task.description:
REQ-ANALYST drafted REQ-005 (FRONTEND-DEV, depends_on [REQ-001a, REQ-001b]: add 'kk' to routing.ts's locales array, keep defaultLocale 'ru', seed messages/kk.json with 177 ru.json-duplicated placeholders) and REQ-006 (CONTENT-BA, depends_on [REQ-005]: write real Kazakh copy, Cyrillic script, Metadata.ogLocale='kk_KZ') into docs/agents/requirements.yaml, in response to GitHub issue #4 ('Add KZ translation'). Run WF-01 Step 2's full gate against both: TESTABILITY, CONSISTENCY, DEPENDS_ON CORRECTNESS, DESIGN-SYSTEM FIT, SIZE. Read both entries directly from docs/agents/requirements.yaml rather than trusting this summary.

Give real scrutiny to the script decision (Cyrillic, not Latin) in REQ-006 -- REQ-ANALYST's reasoning is that Kazakhstan's Latin transition is real but incomplete in practice, so Cyrillic is what the site's actual Kazakh-reading audience reads fluently today, distinct from Uzbek where Latin is Uzbekistan's completed official standard. Assess whether this is a legitimate unilateral call (grounded in a stated, checkable distinction) or should have been escalated as a decisions/ record given it reverses the script-choice pattern set by the one precedent (REQ-002) this project has for a non-Russian locale. Also verify: (a) the locale-count-agnostic claims for request.ts/LocaleSwitcher.tsx/layout.tsx by reading those files yourself, (b) messages/ru.json's current key count matches what REQ-005 assumes (177, not stale), (c) depends_on correctness for both requirements, (d) SIZE -- does REQ-005 (routing edit + seeding) still fit one turn, is the FRONTEND-DEV/CONTENT-BA split still justified at this size per the established REQ-003/REQ-004 precedent.
acceptance_criteria: Checks a-e from WF-01_requirement_development.md Step 2 are each explicitly run and recorded against both REQ-005 and REQ-006

The Cyrillic-vs-Latin script decision is independently assessed with real scrutiny (own reasoning, not just accepting REQ-ANALYST's framing) -- is it a legitimate unilateral call or an escalation case?
The locale-count-agnostic file claims (request.ts, LocaleSwitcher.tsx, layout.tsx) are independently re-verified by reading the actual files
messages/ru.json's current key count independently re-verified (script-based, not assumed)
Any FAIL cites the specific requirement id and check letter
If PASS, result.summary states what was independently re-derived, not just 'looks good'
